detectors.candidate_rule: any metric value is NaN or Inf
detectors.confirmation_rule: CERTAIN: confirms on first observation (no persistence required, because a measured non-finite value cannot be a statistical accident)
known_failure_modes: A persistent non-finite condition previously produced one finding per step; now collapses to one episode by contiguity.
A non-finite value in a metric that is not emitted (sampled out) is invisible.

quality_metrics.note: precision was 0.026 before the episode model and cooldown; see E6_NUMERICS_REPORT.md for the episode-level figure

detectors.candidate_rule: value > min(median(window) * 3.0, quantile(window, 0.995) * 1.5), window excluding warm-up
detectors.confirmation_rule: aggregate series departed, OR cross-layer multiplicity >= 40%, OR peaking >= 8x, OR 2 observations within 5 steps
known_failure_modes: Healthy heavy-tailed gradients: measured 1.25 FP/1k on the H1 class.
Detection boundary between x2 (recall 0.75) and x3 (recall 1.00); not sharp.
A lone layer excursion clears its own envelope easily; mitigated by WEAK classification but present in raw output.

detectors.candidate_rule: detrended robust z-score above spike_z, or value >= relative_factor * window median
detectors.confirmation_rule: 2 observations within 6 steps, or peak ratio >= 6x
known_failure_modes: A real but benign loss spike (a large batch) is indistinguishable from a fault.
Cannot distinguish a data-caused spike from an optimisation-caused one.

detectors.candidate_rule: OLS slope over a trailing window
known_failure_modes: Fires only BEFORE faults: 16 pre-injection false positives.
Never fires inside the acceptable window: recall 0.000 across a magnitude sweep of sustained divergence (1.006, 1.012, 1.03).
A brief positive slope is not divergence; the criterion has no persistence requirement and no baseline normalisation.
detectors.disabled_reason: Measured precision 0.000 and recall 0.000 on the Phase 1.2 holdout. It does not detect the fault it exists for and pollutes default system metrics. LOSS_DIVERGENCE is therefore declared UNSUPPORTED until a persistence-gated, baseline-normalised implementation is validated.

detectors.candidate_rule: step time above a trailing baseline by throughput_drop_ratio for throughput_consecutive steps
known_failure_modes: 9 pre-injection false positives: it alarms during warm-up.
Compares raw step time without normalising for tokens, batch size, sequence length or gradient accumulation.
detectors.disabled_reason: Recall 0.250 with 9 pre-injection false positives. Not usable as a default incident source. THROUGHPUT_REGRESSION is declared UNSUPPORTED in this build.

note: A DISABLED detector is not deleted: historical incidents that reference its detector_id must still resolve, and its measured failure must remain auditable. UNSUPPORTED means no enabled detector can reliably produce that anomaly type in this build.
